name: IGLUE
description: Reliable evaluation benchmarks designed for replicability and comprehensiveness have driven progress in machine learning. Due to the lack of a multilingual benchmark, however, vision-and-language research has mostly focused on English language tasks. To fill this gap, we introduce the Image-Grounded Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark. IGLUE brings together - by both aggregating pre-existing datasets and creating new ones - visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, grounded reasoning, and grounded entailment tasks across 20 diverse languages. Our benchmark enables the evaluation of multilingual multimodal models for transfer learning, not only in a zero-shot setting, but also in newly defined few-shot learning setups. Based on the evaluation of the available state-of-the-art models, we find that translate-test transfer is superior to zero-shot transfer and that few-shot learning is hard to harness for many tasks. Moreover, downstream performance is partially explained by the amount of available unlabelled textual data for pretraining, and only weakly by the typological distance of target-source languages. We hope to encourage future research efforts in this area by releasing the benchmark to the community.
evaluation_method: Task-dependent: accuracy/F1 for VQA and classification, Recall@K for retrieval
general_score_metric: task-dependent (accuracy for classification/VQA; Recall@K for retrieval)
typical_sota_score: varies widely by task and language, commonly ~30–80%
reputation: Well-regarded for multilingual multimodal evaluation; increasingly used in vision-and-language research for non-English settings.
notes: Multilingual construction can introduce translation/artifact noise; downstream performance varies strongly with language-resource availability; not uniformly saturated across tasks/languages.
